subject: Sprint-to-QBR: topline signals, critical mitigations, and two-week asks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint-to-QBR: topline signals, critical mitigations, and two-week asks

Good morning — sending a compact operational snapshot for this sprint as we finalize the QBR deck. Key highlights below (actionable asks at the end). Slides attached (QBR_slide_v2.pdf) and full deck in the Drive link.

Topline signals
- Hosted API latency: 95th %-tile spiked to 320ms on Wed (baseline ~220ms) during the EU batch; traced to a misconfigured autoscaler policy on Dedicated overflow routing.
- Cost per 1k tokens for chat workloads dropped 7% after the new quantization profile rollout (early signal looks good).
- Two notable security/compliance asks from Acme: SOC2 attestation timeline confirmation and an SLA exception for cross-region failover (details below).

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: If Dedicated overflow continues routing to older kernel builds, we could see repeated latency spikes into QBR week. Mitigation: Infra will pin overflow pool to vetted kernel build for the next 72 hours and run a synthetic load at 30% higher throughput tonight (Jonas to own).
- Risk: Acme procurement timeline is tight — they requested a contract start aligned with their FY on Aug 24. If legal redlines linger, they’ve flagged potential push to an alternate vendor. Mitigation: Sales to prioritize the redline call this week; finance to pre-approve a one-time credit if needed.
- Risk: One customer reported degraded rerank accuracy after optimizer change. Mitigation: Rollback option staged; Research to run A/B on 8/8.

Two-week asks (concise)
1) Jonas: run pinned overflow test tonight and share 1-2 slides with latency curves by 10:00 PDT tomorrow.
2) Karthik + Legal: finalize response to Acme’s SLA exception request (attach SLA_exception_request.docx) and confirm whether we can approve a temporary exception for cross-region failover by 8/12.
3) Laura: QBR narrative review — I’ve flagged 3 slides that need tone softening around capacity. Can you make edits and return by EOD 8/9?
4) Marissa: set up a 30-min sync with Acme GTM + Procurement (Emily + procurement contact) to close commercial terms — prefer Wed 8/11 afternoon.

Quick notes: I propose we move slide 6 (cost curves) to the appendix and surface Karthik’s SLA recommendation front-and-center. If anyone needs a different allocation of asks, reply inline.

Thanks — V

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Global Operations | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

Attachments: QBR_slide_v2.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-to-QBR: topline signals, critical mitigations, and two-week asks

Thanks Vanessa — quick updates / clarifying Qs inline.

- SLA exception: I’ve reviewed Acme’s requested language. We can approve a temporary cross-region failover exception if we add two controls: 1) a 30-day notice window for planned cross-region failover and 2) an SLO-weighted credit schedule (cap at 10% spend for first quarter). I’ll draft the redline and attach it to Legal this afternoon.
- Budget/credits: Finance asks for a one-page justification for the credit; Marissa, can you prep a short rationale (1 paragraph) after the Acme sync?
- Rerank regression: Research should pause the optimizer push to prod until A/B confirms. If Research needs rollback help, Infra can schedule the window tonight.

I’ll circulate the SLA redline (SLA_exception_request.docx) by 16:00. If leadership is okay with the temporary controls above, we can close commercial terms faster.

—Karthik
Director, Commercial Operations
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:57:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-to-QBR: topline signals, critical mitigations, and two-week asks

Acknowledged. I ran an initial overflow test at 09:30 and saw the tail latency reduce from 320ms to ~230ms after pinning the overflow pool to build r9.4. I’ll run the 30% higher throughput synthetic tonight (22:00 PDT) and upload the graphs to the Drive. Expect a 1-slide summary by 10:00 PDT tomorrow.

Also: I recommend we keep the rollback plan on standby for the rerank optimizer; Research, please confirm target metric thresholds for an automatic rollback.

-Jonas
Head of Infrastructure
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: GTM Lead - Acme AI <g.garcia@acme.ai>, procurement@nebulacloud.com
Date: 2026-08-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-to-QBR: topline signals, critical mitigations, and two-week asks

Thanks Vanessa and team — appreciate the fast follow. We can meet Wed 8/11 at 2:00 PM PDT for the procurement + GTM sync (Marissa, please send the calendar invite). Acme legal is comfortable reviewing a temporary exception with the controls Karthik outlined. Procurement asked for the final SLA redline by EOD 8/10 to route internally in time for an Aug 24 start.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the QBR deck will include a migration/cutover playbook for cross-region failover? If so, please surface it as an appendix slide.
- We’d like a short note on rollback SLAs if rerank is rolled back mid-quarter.

Emily Zhang
Head of Partnerships, Acme AI
emily.zhang@acme.ai
